headline: 女性主義先驅史坦能辭世
context: 美國女性主義先驅葛羅莉亞・史坦能（Gloria Steinem）辭世，享耆壽92歲，希拉蕊・柯林頓等政治人物與名人紛紛致哀。藝文圈另外有幾部新作在威尼斯影展亮相：導演馬丁・麥多納的新片找來約翰・馬克維奇與山姆・洛克威爾主演，紀錄片則回顧了紐西蘭已故橄欖球傳奇喬納・洛姆的一生。斯洛伐克新星Adéla也推出首張專輯，直白唱出樂壇的浮華與算計。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: His destructive pace and power changed the game for ever, but behind the fame and impassive exterior of this gentle giant was a life of chaos and emotional discord There’s an inevitable air of melancholy overhanging this profile of New Zealand rugby star Jonah Lomu; we all know how the story ended for this magnificent human specimen, who died in 2015 aged 40 as a result of a longterm kidney disorder. Lomu, of course, became a legend of the game after breaking into the All Blacks side – the ferociously high-achieving New Zealand national team, for anyone outside the rugby-appreciating universe – at the scarcely believable age of 19; his special combination of a tank-like physique, electric pace and ability to slalom at high speed gave him an almost unstoppable force in what is arguably the toughest contact sport of all. Lomu had the bulk and power of a forward (I liked the detail that he was sometimes drafted into the back of the scrum when they needed “more power”) but he was set loose on the wing, where he was twice the speed and three times the size of everyone else, and where his destructive instincts could wreak havoc. Well, modern rugby appears to have learned the Lomu lesson; everyone has bulked up – so its arguable whether he would have the same impact today. But as this film underlines, there was a lot more to Lomu’s story than steamrolling the hapless English backline; he had a complicated relationship both with his Tongan heritage and his superstar status, the combination of which seemed to overwhelm him. Interestingly, this film (directed by Gavin Fitzgerald and Vea Mafile’o) initially appears to push the by-now customary idea that Lomu’s Indigenous heritage was an ineffable source of strength, wisdom and insight; however it soon becomes clear that this wasn’t entirely the case. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: (Polydor) The 22-year-old is impressively frank about indulging industry sleaze in her pursuit of fame on a debut that puts a distinctive spin on the best of 00s hedonism There’s something very striking about hearing a pop star in 2026, their voice larded with Auto-Tune, opening a song with the line “I can’t really sing”. We live in an era where fans seem more aware than ever of the nefarious music business machinations that lurk within the star-making process, one where you’re never far away from online outrage decrying some artist or other as an industry plant. Nevertheless, admitting that the ubiquitous audio processing software is sometimes deployed for a helping hand, not a futuristic aesthetic, feels strangely jarring. On one hand, well of course it is. On the other, actually announcing that without it, you might be honking like a despondent goose, in the first line of a song, still amounts to a dramatic breaking of the fourth wall. That said, it’s very much on brand for Adéla Jergová, who started her career as a contestant on a TV talent show – she failed to make the cut for crumbling “global girl group” Katseye, as documented on Netflix’s Pop Star Academy – before established names alighted on her as a more left-field solo proposition: Grimes co-produced her early single Machine Girl. New artists are well advised to have a USP, something that helps them cut through the mass of peers vying for public attention on streaming services. The 22-year-old Slovakian has chosen to differentiate herself from the serried ranks of post-Brat female pop stars by spiking her songs about hedonism and messy sexual encounters (“no bed frame, we can do it on the carpet … you eat real good for a starving artist”) with a kind of meta commentary on what it is to be a female pop star. sources.summary: Prolific author campaigned against domestic violence, female genital mutilation, pornography and the Vietnam and Gulf wars ‘We badly need to raise our boys more like our girls’: Gloria Steinem – a life in quotes Hillary Clinton leads tributes to Gloria Steinem: ‘Her activism was rooted in optimism’ Gloria Steinem, the American feminist and journalist whose activism helped push through greater rights for women around the world has died, aged 92. Steinem “passed away peacefully at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her”, a statement shared to her Instagram page said. Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Venice film festival: Two men, some violence, much freewheeling chat: so far, so standard fare from the Oscar-winning writer-director. But this time the comedy and charm can feel diluted by blood and machismo It isn’t a Martin McDonagh movie unless you’ve got two morose guys – one old, one not so old – who do nothing all the livelong day but bitch and snipe and quarrel and exchange barbed bromantic dialogue while occasionally going off on a plaintive tangent about nothing at all, incidentally revealing something very wrong with their friendship. If it can be called that. In The Banshees of Inisherin from 2022 , the older guy decides he wants nothing more to do with the younger guy; in In Bruges from 14 years earlier (of which this latest film is almost a retread or maybe B-side), the older guy has an awful secret he is keeping from the younger guy. Wild Horse Nine brings McDonagh to a US setting with American (not Irish) characters and dialogue. But as in another US-set film – 2012’s Seven Psychopaths – Americanness can bring out something less interesting in McDonagh: more violence, more strenuous sweary machismo, less comedy, less charm. Yet there is something interesting and watchably acrid in the pairing of Sam Rockwell and John Malkovich, with Malkovich unspooling long speeches in that unmistakable nasal croon or whine, often concluding with his lips parted in a pursed-lip pout, a mannerism that leaves the audience unsure exactly how ironic or contemptuous he is supposed to sound. 美國女性主義先驅史坦能辭世 享耆壽92。美國女性主義先驅葛羅莉亞・史坦能（Gloria Steinem）辭世，享耆壽92歲，希拉蕊・柯林頓等政治人物與名人紛紛致哀。藝文圈這邊還有幾則消息：威尼斯影展上，導演馬丁・麥多納的新片找來約翰・馬克維奇與山姆・洛克威爾主演，紀錄片也回顧了紐西蘭已故橄欖球傳奇喬納・洛姆的一生，斯洛伐克新星Adéla則推出首張專輯，直白唱出樂壇的浮華與算計。

threads_text:
美國女性主義先驅葛羅莉亞・史坦能（Gloria Steinem）辭世，享耆壽92歲。她的Instagram帳號發出聲明說，她在紐約家中安詳離世，身邊圍繞著許多愛她的人；希拉蕊・柯林頓、梅根馬克爾、蓮娜・丹恩等名人與政治人物，紛紛悼念她數十年來為女性權益發聲的貢獻。藝文圈這邊還有幾則消息：威尼斯影展上，導演馬丁・麥多納的新片《Wild Horse Nine》找來約翰・馬克維奇與山姆・洛克威爾主演；一部紀錄片回顧了已故紐西蘭橄欖球傳奇喬納・洛姆的一生，他在2015年因腎臟疾病過世，得年40歲；22歲的斯洛伐克歌手Adéla也推出首張專輯，直白唱出自己在樂壇打滾時經歷的浮華與算計。

本則整理自 The Guardian 與 The New York Times 於 2026 年 9 月 3、4 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 美國女性主義先驅葛羅莉亞・史坦能過世了，享耆壽92歲。她在紐約家中安詳離世，身邊圍繞著許多愛她的人，許多名人與政治人物都在悼念她幾十年來為女性權益發聲的貢獻。藝術這邊也有幾件事。威尼斯影展上，有一部新片找來兩位資深男星主演，說的是兩個怪咖男人的公路故事；還有一部紀錄片，回顧了紐西蘭已故橄欖球傳奇球星喬納・洛姆的一生，他因為腎臟疾病，在40歲那年過世；一位22歲的斯洛伐克新星也發了首張專輯，直白唱出自己在樂壇打滾遇到的浮華與算計。
